raw.title: Founding UI/UX Designer, Unannounced Game
raw.description:
This is your opportunity to join a small group of obsessed game makers, building an ambitious mobile game focused on collection and social.

As our founding UI & UX Designer, you will be the owner of the entire UX structure at a high level, down to the UI art pixels in detail. You will work intimately with engineers, artists, designers from the vision level, down to the hands on implementation. Not settling for industry good, but pioneering new UX paradigms, head turning UI art style and hyper juicy interactions.

We’re looking for someone who is passionate about their craft, making social game experiences, and also a student of behavioral psychology. Someone who plays games seriously, but understands that at least a bit of silliness is needed for success. Someone who thinks about all the edge cases, but knows doing it alone, will always leave blind spots. If you feel you have great ability, a growth mindset, and high ambition, then join us at the start of our journey!

Side quest: Read this new page about making new games at Supercell.

What You'll Be Doing

  • UX flow design for entire game experience

  • Creation and implementation of UI screens, assets and animations

  • Involved in pioneering a modern workflow and optimise assets for performance

  • Discover and manage external partners where needed

What You Have

  • 5+ years of experience shipping UI/UX design for apps/games

  • Portfolio showcasing end-to-end UI/UX work on game projects, with examples of UI and UX flows

  • Proven ability to translate game design requirements into intuitive and visually stunning UI solutions

  • Experience collaborating closely with engineers, game designers and artists

  • Passionate about both UI & UX design

  • Range of 2D Art skills (UI elements, illustrations, animations, etc.)

  • Proficient understanding of Graphic Design and Typography

  • A self-starter approach to use AI: you've found ways to use it in your day-to-day work, you experiment, figure things out and bring the same energy to every new challenge.

Would Be Nice if You Also Have

  • At the forefront with AI tools and actively experimenting

  • Enjoys TCGs

Where You'll Be

This opportunity is based in our London office, and because we value a collaborative work environment and genuine human interactions, it is mostly an office‑based role.

Supercell New Games

This is a dedicated environment for building from zero and shaped around a core belief: the best developers don’t need more direction, they need more freedom and fewer barriers. This is where games get the space they need to become cultural phenomenons.

Players are waiting for your vision and ambition to build the next forever game a.k.a. the best work of your career. We back this up with creative and operational autonomy, and the infrastructure, capital, and experience needed to take a game from an idea to global scale.

This is not for everyone. Building towards a billion-dollar game is going to be hard. But let's not kid ourselves: it should also be fun.

You build the rocket. We bring the launchpad.

Game-changing Financial Model

Supercell is great with stuff around benefits and wellbeing, but most importantly you get to focus on what matters: making games. Skip the Venture Capital pitch decks and looking at runway spreadsheets. In exchange, we're offering a compensation model that makes this opportunity financially life-changing.

About Supercell

Supercell is a games company from Helsinki, Finland, with offices also in San Francisco, Seoul, Shanghai, and London. You might know us as the makers of Hay Day, Clash of Clans, Boom Beach, Clash Royale, and Brawl Stars. Our mission is to create great games that as many people as possible play for years and that are remembered forever.

So, how do we make great games? By putting together the best teams and giving them the freedom and independence to succeed. And by taking risks, failing, sharing learnings, and killing lots of projects.

Relocation? Yes!

No matter where you’re moving from, our dedicated mobility team and partners will support you throughout your move. We’ll ensure the process is as smooth as possible for you and anyone joining you – whether they’re family members of the human or animal kind!

raw.description:
Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.

As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.

Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion.   • You can work end to end. Comfortable owning the server side as well as the front end: SSR, serverless and edge runtimes, API routes, a SQL database, secrets and CI. You should be able to take a feature from schema to component to the route that serves it without handing off, and be happy debugging something that only reproduces in production.

  • Solid understanding of responsive design, cross-browser compatibility and web performance, and comfortable building to WCAG 2.2 AA. Accessibility is part of your definition of done, not a separate pass.

  • You care that marketing sites are measured, on performance, SEO, analytics events and conversion, and you're happy being accountable to those numbers.

  • A strong sense of craft and attention to detail, and the judgement to balance design intent against engineering constraints.

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills. You explain your reasoning, review generously, and treat levelling up the people around you as part of the job.

Nice to haves

  • Prior experience working on a large SaaS marketing website, at real traffic and with real stakes attached.

  • Astro, or another islands or static-site framework.

  • Cloudflare Workers, or another edge or serverless platform.

  • Experience with AWS Lambda.

  • Tailwind CSS v4, and experience working from a token-based design system.

  • Experience, or strong interest, in making component libraries and content models consumable by AI agents.

  • A strong design sensibility: an eye for visual detail and the judgement to push back on and improve design decisions, not just build them.

  • Experience with localisation and internationalisation at scale for a global audience.

  • Analytics and tag management implementation: dataLayer events, server-side tagging, getting attribution right without hurting performance.

Our culture

At Synthesia we're passionate about building, not talking, planning or politicising. We strive to hire the smartest, kindest and most unrelenting people and let them do their best work without distractions. Our work principles serve as our charter for how we make decisions, give feedback and structure our work to empower everyone to go as fast as possible. You can find out more about these principles here.

The hiring process:

  • 30 min call with our Technical Recruiter

  • 45 min call with the Head of Website about your past projects

  • 75 min practical exercise with one of our engineers. We hand you a real Figma section spec and work through how you'd model and build it. Collaborative, not Leetcode.

  • 60 min call with leadership, focused on examples of collaboration, growth, and the details of your future team.

Other important info:

  • Our preference is for this role to be based either in-office or remote in London, UK. We can also accommodate remote workers elsewhere in Europe subject to compliance and right to work checks.

  • This is full-time employment only, usually through OysterHR. No contractors possible.

Senior People Partner (all genders)
raw.description:
About tonies:

tonies is the world’s leading interactive audio platform for children, with over 12 million Tonieboxes and 165 million Tonies sold globally. Our intuitive, screen-free system empowers children to learn and play independently in a safe and engaging way.

With a presence in over 100 countries and a diverse portfolio of ~1,500 Tonies across multiple languages, we continue to redefine how children experience storytelling and learning. Since our IPO in 2021, our global team of 630+ colleagues is united by a shared mission: shaping the future of play, learning, and imagination.


You as part of tonies:

At tonies, storytelling is at the heart of everything we do. Our success isn't just about innovative technology and creative ideas – it's about the passionate, talented people who bring those stories to life. As we scale, we are looking for a Senior People Partner to join our journey and shape our next chapter. In this role, you’ll be part of our People Partnering team, with the ambition to build high-impact teams through collaborative partnerships and a high-performance culture as an engine for long-term business success


Your tasks and responsibilities will include:

Driving Organizational Effectiveness through Strategic People Partnering

  • Partner closely with leadership in your designated area across various levels, acting as a trusted strategic advisor on a broad range of people and organizational matters.
  • Support the evolution of your area by contributing to organizational design matters and the implementation of structural changes.

Coaching Leaders to Lead with Impact
  • Act as a coach and sparring partner to leaders, supporting their leadership effectiveness.
  • Help leaders navigate organizational and cultural change, make thoughtful leadership decisions, and drive high-performance within their teams.

Driving the Implementation of People Programs
  • Partner with the people development function to drive the implementation and adoption of people programs within your designated area.
  • Support leaders and teams through change and take ownership of core programs, e.g performance feedback, ensuring effective delivery and desired outcomes.

Navigating Employee Relations with Empathy and Expertise
  • Support the resolution of employee relations matters, including conflict resolution, disciplinary actions, and sensitive workplace dynamics (either directly or in close collaboration with our Employee Relations Specialist).
  • Ensure situations are handled thoughtfully, consistently, and in line with our values and legal requirements.

Creating a Seamless Employee Experience through Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner closely with cross-functional People & Culture teams to ensure a seamless employee experience and embed cohesive ways of working between the business and our department.


What we are looking for:

  • Multiple years of experience as a People Partner in a complex global company, ideally in a fast-paced, scaling context, with deep experience in partnering with leaders across different countries, including the US.
  • Strong business acumen and strategic thinking to understand how different business areas operate, connect people priorities with business needs, and confidently act as a trusted advisor to leaders.
  • Strong collaboration and cross-functional partnership skills, working effectively as a team player with stakeholders at multiple levels across the organization.
  • Clear, confident, and empathetic communication, stakeholder management, and influencing skills, with the ability to adapt to different audiences, build trusted relationships, and create alignment on complex or sensitive topics.
  • Action-oriented ownership to proactively drive topics forward, navigate obstacles, and ensure initiatives are successfully implemented to achieve desired outcomes.
  • Skilled at systemic thinking and problem-solving, understanding how people, processes, and structures interconnect to identify underlying patterns and develop thoughtful, sustainable solutions.
  • Global mindset and flexibility to thrive in an international setup, including early-evening meetings when needed to collaborate with US-based colleagues as well as occasional business trips to Düsseldorf
  • Ideally, experience working with works councils and navigating the associated processes and requirements.


Why tonies?

●   Global Teamwork: We collaborate across departmental and country borders. You’ll be part of a truly international community where every voice is heard.
●   Come as you are: This applies to the dress code and everything else. We believe you give your best when you feel truly comfortable being yourself.
●   Competitive Package: We offer a competitive salary and a range of comprehensive benefits tailored to your specific location, which we’ll share during the recruiting process.
●   Collaboration & Community: We’re big on "we." You’ll join a team that values connection and celebrates wins together, no matter the time zone.
●   Continuous Learning: Benefit from internal/external training and an individual learning budget to keep your skills as sharp as a Tonie’s ears.
●   Tonie Discounts: Enjoy attractive discounts on our entire range of products. You’ll quickly become the favorite guest at every birthday party!
●   Rest & Recharge: Great work requires a clear head. You’ll enjoy generous paid time off to ensure you have plenty of time for your own stories.


Good to know:

As part of our principles, we are committed to supporting inclusion and diversity at tonies. We actively celebrate our colleagues’ different abilities, ethnicities, faith and gender. Everyone is welcome and supported in their development at all stages in their journey with us. 

We look forward to hearing from you!

Sabine Schykowski
Talent Acquisition Manager

raw.description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

We're looking for a Data Scientist to take ownership of the datasets and evaluation workflows that underpin our AI Safety work. You'll turn real-world product data into reliable, well-structured datasets for training and evaluating models, and help build the processes and infrastructure to continuously assess how those models perform in production.

This is a hands-on role at the intersection of data science, ML, AI safety, and policy. You'll work closely with safety researchers, engineers, and policy specialists to translate complex safety requirements into practical data and evaluation systems - starting hands-on with collection, analysis, and labelling, then building the methodologies, contributor networks, and quality standards that let this work scale.

In this role, you will

  • Own safety datasets end-to-end: collection, cleaning, labelling, quality control, versioning, and readiness for training and evaluation.

  • Translate safety policy into clear, consistent labelling and evaluation criteria, working closely with policy specialists.

  • Design and manage labelling processes, including sourcing, onboarding, and overseeing external contributors to a high quality bar.

  • Build evaluation workflows for models in production, using real-world data to track performance and surface issues.

  • Develop lightweight Python/SQL pipelines and tooling to make data work faster and reproducible, partnering with ML engineers on what "training-ready" looks like.

Who you are

  • Experience as a Data Scientist, or similar, working with real-world datasets and ML models.

  • Strong grasp of what makes a good dataset: collection, cleaning, sampling, labelling, quality control, evaluation.

  • Comfortable with Python and SQL for analysis and practical data workflows.

  • Strong critical thinking and judgement - comfortable with ambiguity and nuance, and able to turn complex guidelines into consistent, scalable decisions.

  • Autonomous and a clear communicator, able to work across disciplines (policy, engineering, research) in a fast-moving, still-forming environment.

Bonus points

  • Experience in AI safety, trust & safety, content moderation, or fraud/abuse detection.

  • Experience building datasets or evaluation frameworks, or with adversarial/safety-focused ML.

  • Experience managing human-in-the-loop labelling processes, dataset versioning, or ML pipeline tooling.

  • Experience operationalising guidelines with policy or legal teams.

Location

This role is based in London, where you'll work closely with our AI Safety and Policy teams.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

About the role

ElevenLabs spends meaningfully on paid acquisition, and that spend is only as good as the data behind it. We are looking for an engineer to own our measurement layer end to end: the tag manager setup, the tracking and attribution scripts on our sites, and the server-to-server conversion tracking that feeds our ad platforms.

Day to day you will work closely with the paid marketing team: fixing tracking bugs as they come in, setting up tracking for new landing pages and campaigns, and debugging discrepancies between platform-reported conversions and our internal data. Longer term, you will define how tracking should properly work here and build the monitoring so we catch breakage in hours, not weeks.

This role sits between frontend engineering, data engineering, and marketing. You will add and improve tracking scripts without hurting pagespeed, keep our server-side GTM container healthy, make sure consent and regional restrictions are correctly enforced, and ensure the right channels get credit for the right conversions. Your work directly decides how a large paid budget gets allocated.

What you will do

  • Own our tag manager setup end to end, including the server-side GTM container, and review any changes other teams want to make

  • Work with the paid marketing team daily: fix tracking bugs, set up tracking for new landing pages and campaigns, and debug discrepancies between platform-reported conversions and our internal data

  • Build and maintain server-to-server conversion tracking (Meta CAPI, Google Enhanced Conversions, and similar) and validate pixel vs server deduplication

  • Improve tracking script performance and correctness, keeping script impact on pagespeed and Core Web Vitals within budget

  • Make sure consent handling and regional restrictions are correctly enforced across markets

  • Define event schema and UTM conventions, and document them so tracking for new campaigns is correct by default

  • Build monitoring and alerting for the measurement stack so we catch broken tracking within hours, not weeks

  • Review PRs that add conversion events to the main app, and work with product engineering on tracking integrations

Requirements

  • Strong JavaScript/TypeScript, comfortable working in both frontend code and a production application codebase

  • Hands-on experience with Google Tag Manager, including server-side GTM, and at least one conversion API (Meta CAPI, Google Enhanced Conversions, or similar) implemented server-to-server

  • Experience debugging attribution discrepancies end to end: pixel vs server deduplication, UTM conventions, event schema design

  • Solid understanding of web performance and how to add tracking without degrading Core Web Vitals

  • Working knowledge of consent and privacy requirements (Consent Mode v2, regional restrictions) and SQL for validating tracking data in the warehouse

Bonus

  • CDP experience (Segment, RudderStack, Snowplow)

  • Product analytics tools (GA4, Amplitude, PostHog) and dbt

  • Next.js experience

  • Exposure to incrementality testing or media mix modelling

Growth potential

We believe in hiring the best talent in the world to make an impact in the right role at the right time. At ElevenLabs, strong performance creates opportunities for growth. Here are some of the career paths you can expect after excelling in this role:

  • Own the whole martech and measurement area as it grows, potentially leading a small marketing engineering team

  • Grow toward senior/staff IC on the engineering track

  • Broaden into data engineering and attribution modelling, or into growth engineering more widely (experimentation, landing page infrastructure)

Location

This role is remote and can be executed globally. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London, New York, Madrid, Warsaw and many more.

AI Safety Manager
raw.description:
Slingshot AI

Slingshot AI is the team behind Ash, the first AI designed for mental health. Our mission is to make support more accessible and help people change their lives in the ways they want.

We’re building a world-class team by empowering individuals with the autonomy, flexibility, and support they need to do their best work. We dream big, iterate fast, and care deeply. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.

Our team spans machine learning, product, engineering, conversational design, clinical, growth, and operations, with offices in both New York City and London.

We're a well-funded Series A company, having raised $93M from Andreessen Horowitz, Radical Ventures, Forerunner Ventures, plus top-tier tech investors involved in ElevenLabs, Captions, Shopify, Plaid, Notion, Canva, Twitch, Airtable, and many others.

The role

We’re hiring a leader to help shape how we approach trust and safety at Ash, in our model and in our product.

People bring deeply personal things to Ash. That creates difficult questions about how the product should behave, how we respond when something goes wrong, and how we protect people while respecting their privacy and autonomy. You’ll work alongside psychologists, researchers, and machine learning engineers to develop novel systems for AI in a sensitive domain.

You’ll help us answer hard, ambiguous questions about our model’s policy, investigate, research, develop new policies, and implement them, and communicate clearly about them to both internal and external audiences.

The role combines strategy, hands-on operations, and communication. You might spend one day working through a difficult safety decision with our clinical and legal teams, the next building a process for handling user reports, and the next writing an explanation of our approach for the public.

We’re looking for a thoughtful generalist who learns quickly, makes things happen, and cares deeply about getting this right.

What you’ll do

  • Develop our principles and policies. Work through questions where safety, privacy, user autonomy, and product usefulness pull in different directions. Research the problem, seek expert input, and make a reasoned recommendation. You’ll work with our team, our advisors and experts and others to build principles for how to handle decisions.

  • Turn ambiguous issues into clear decisions. Investigate user reports, emerging risks, and new requirements. Establish what we know, what remains uncertain, and what we should do next.

  • Make the response work in practice. Build clear processes for triage, investigation, escalation, and follow-through. Define who does what, create the tools and documentation they need, and handle the operational details yourself.

  • Turn learning into product improvements. Work with engineering, machine learning, clinical, and legal colleagues to translate findings into changes to Ash and the systems around it.

  • Build, test, and improve quickly. For new systems, put a useful first version in place, learn from real cases, and refine it. Match the pace and level of review to the consequences of the decision.

  • Write clearly, internally and externally. Produce policies, practical guidance, and public explanations of our safety approach. Help communicate our evaluations and findings, including their limitations. You’ll build initiatives or benchmarks we can share with the outside world to help us and the industry at large do better.

  • Represent our thinking. Explain and defend our approach with partners, clinicians, and other audiences. Engage seriously with criticism and bring what you learn back into the work.

About you

  • You have strong judgment. You can reason through a difficult question, weigh competing considerations, and recommend a course of action without pretending every answer is certain.

  • You’re an excellent writer and communicator. You can turn complex thinking into clear, precise prose. You enjoy doing the research and developing the argument as much as writing the final piece. You can present well and understand how to communicate what we’re doing to the outside world.

  • You’ve built something and made it better. It could be a product, an operational process, a program, or an independent project. You can show how you moved from an unclear problem to something people used, then improved it through feedback.

  • You’re resourceful and hands-on. You’re willing to investigate individual cases, coordinate people, write the checklist, and follow up until the work is done.

  • You seek out expertise without needing someone else to supply every answer. You know when to consult a clinician, engineer, lawyer, or researcher, and can turn their input into a practical decision.

  • You’re intellectually curious and willing to change your mind. You can explain a time when evidence challenged your assumptions and changed your approach.

  • You handle sensitive information with care and stay thoughtful under pressure. You recognize that this role will involve handling difficult topics on a regular basis including abuse, eating disorders, suicide and death. You can handle these topics maturely and know how to manage your own mental health, seeking support for yourself as needed.

  • You care deeply about people’s mental health and the opportunity in front of us. You want more people to have access to good support, and you take responsibility for the trust that requires.

You might come from product, operations, consulting, law, policy, psychology, cognitive science, or another field that has taught you to think rigorously, write well, and execute. Clinical qualifications and previous trust and safety experience are useful, but neither is required.

The role

We are seeking a Creative Strategy Lead to join the Slingshot AI marketing team. Reporting to our head of growth, your job is to identify, create, test, and scale our D2C creative motion. Millions of people already use general purpose AI as a therapist, and millions more are on a waitlist or priced out of care. Demand is not our problem. Getting Ash in front of the people who need it is. Creative is the biggest lever we have on that, and this role owns it.

This is a hands-on role by design. You own the loop, coming up with creative copy, producing visuals and tag-lines, and iterating quickly to dial in on what works. You are building the engine that gets Ash in front of people. You create and test fast, trust your instincts, and want to develop the playbook that puts proper mental healthcare at the world's fingertips.

Key responsibilities:

  • Own the weekly experiment loop: hypothesis, A/B test, read the result, identify winners, iterate. This is the spine of the role and where taste shows up.

  • Build the system that makes it repeatable. Testing cadence, angle library, naming and tagging, and a bank of real user language pulled from communities, reviews, and our own conversations.

  • Create winning concepts and then raise the hit rate of winning concepts so paid has more to scale behind. The bar is quality, not volume, and you manage what we spend proving things out.

  • Write the hooks, headlines, overlays, and scripts, in the voice of the person scrolling.

  • Brief at volume: one brief that many creators each interpret their own way, built for what each network rewards rather than resizing one idea for all of them.

  • Coach creators with sharp feedback, one to many. You brief and evaluate and if required can do creator ops, supporting in producing the content yourself.

  • Work with media buying on a weekly cadence. You read media buy KPIs and go into the buying tools yourself to check how tests performed, and you know buying well enough to challenge the buyer on their own ground.

  • Develop the product and audience understanding that decides what works. When AI makes output cheap, this becomes the deciding factor in paid.

  • Set the visual and verbal point of view for Ash in market. We do not look like the rest of this category, and we do not intend to start.

About you:

  • You produce assets yourself on the AI stack, Figma, CapCut and the rest. Not in front of the camera, but you make the creative for testing, not just brief it.

  • You come from the paid side moving into creative, or creative moving toward paid. Both work. What matters is turning product and audience understanding into creative that wins.

  • Experienced in writing performance copy; have taste and can quickly iterate

  • Consumer only, ideally subscription. If your background is SaaS, this is not the role.

  • You can set up a clean test, say in advance what would prove you wrong, read the result honestly, and defend your taste with an argument rather than a mood board.

  • You want to work on mental health for a reason you can say out loud.

Nice to have:

  • You can challenge our media buyer on their own ground, because you have done the buying yourself.

  • You have built or reshaped web funnels and landing pages to match the creative that drove the click.

  • You have built or run a creator or UGC pipeline, including sourcing, briefing, and quality control.

raw.description:
Slingshot AI

Slingshot AI is the team behind Ash, the first AI designed for mental health. Our mission is to make support more accessible and help people change their lives in the ways they want.

We’re building a world-class team by empowering individuals with the autonomy, flexibility, and support they need to do their best work. We dream big, iterate fast, and care deeply. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.

Our team spans machine learning, product, engineering, conversational design, clinical, growth, and operations, with offices in both New York City and London.

We're a well-funded Series A company, having raised $93M from Andreessen Horowitz, Radical Ventures, Forerunner Ventures, plus top-tier tech investors involved in ElevenLabs, Captions, Shopify, Plaid, Notion, Canva, Twitch, Airtable, and many others.

The Role

We are hiring a Product Psychologist to sit inside our machine learning team to elaborate on and help further build processes that answer: what does a great Ash conversation look like, and how do you measure it?

Reporting to our Clinical R&D Lead and partnering closely our ML conversation team lead, you'll own the definition of quality for Ash's conversations and turn it into something the ML team can train and evaluate against through benchmarks, evals, and a distributed team of expert human reviewers.

We think optimizing for clinical protocols is the wrong lever. We believe the core driver of outcomes in mental health support, AI or human, is more amorphous: the things that set individual practitioners, rather than individual practices, apart. This role exists to build a science of that belief into something iterable.

This is not a role about designing conversations turn-by-turn. Ash is more grown than built. It's not a management role, though you'll coach a growing team of reviewers. And it's not a research role in the traditional sense. While you'll draw heavily on the literature, your aim is product outcomes, not papers published (though some of your work may become a paper in collaboration with our research team).

Key responsibilities

  • Own the definition of "great" for Ash conversations, and make it measurable.

  • Make hypothesis-driven calls on how Ash should behave, globally and in specific situations. Change your mind quickly and openly when the evidence tells you to.

  • Partner with the Safety team to define Ash's constraints and how it should handle difficult edge-case conversations.

  • Recruit, scale, and coach a distributed team of human reviewers: set the bar, teach people what "great" looks like, and keep the group calibrated with each other.

  • Be a source of clarity for the conversation and ML teams when the path forward is ambiguous.

About you

  • You have a PhD in Clinical or Counseling Psychology, or related field, or a license-eligible Masters degree with clinical training and supervision

  • You’re an experienced clinician with a history of working with systems, technological and otherwise, to scale up engaging and effective health products

  • You have deep, hands-on experience with interpersonal skills. You can personally facilitate emotional expression well, and you can also see it in someone else's work: flexibility, warmth, honesty, confidence, and attunement, not just credentials.

  • You're pragmatic and decisive under real uncertainty. You can make a call with incomplete information, defend it, and drop it fast when new evidence shows up.

  • You're oriented toward the user, not toward an external clinical ideal. You won't push an agenda that matters more to you than it does to the people using the product.

  • You've worked on measurement before, ideally in digital mental health, and you know how to build a rating system and keep a team of raters calibrated.

  • You have some comfort operating close to an ML team. You don't need to train the models, but you should be curious about how evals and benchmarks actually get used to change model behavior.

Compensation: £80K – £100K

About Smartnumbers

We are on a mission to stop fraud and improve customer authentication. Fraud is a huge problem affecting millions of people, it costs the UK nearly £7bn and represents 40% of all crime. Too often the solution has been to put in place cumbersome authentication processes that frustrate genuine customers, cause inefficiencies for organisations and fail to prevent fraud. 
 
We are changing this by providing organisations with real-time insight into the risk of a caller. We combine patented machine learning technology with our industry consortium to help identify and prevent contact centre fraud. We also provide clients with real-time insight into the authenticity of the call by leveraging our unique network access and relationships. 
 
We recognise that we need to work together to fight fraud, that is why we have fostered strategic partnerships with leading global organisations like Amazon, BT, and Genesys. Together, we protect some of the UKs largest banks, insurance companies and emergency services. We also believe in developing our people into high performing teams.


What you'll be working on

We're looking for someone to build out a long term 2–3 year strategic pipeline. As part of the role, you will be expected to do the following: 
 

  • Build and maintain a 12–18 month active pipeline to support business objectives
  • Build and maintain relevant market awareness through client discussions, market research and industry events
  • Provide senior management with clear updates, progress and forecasts as evidenced through the company CRM
  • Nurture the customer advocacy program in support of our broader business goals
  • Prioritise activities to meet quarterly business targets while maintaining a longer-term strategic pipeline

What you’ll achieve 

You’ll be helping us achieve our mission by enabling fraud investigators across organisations to collaborate in their fight against fraud using our SaaS platform. The types of areas you’ll look at include: 
  • New Business Development
  • Leading client facing discover conversations to establish key business issues
  • Understanding and navigating the different approaches to fraud prevention across different sectors
  • Helping Clients build business cases for Smartnumbers adoption
  • Sharing intelligence and best practice across organisations
  • Increasing market awareness by supporting events, posts or other GTM activities
  • Building trust and a network of advocates among your client base

How you’ll work 

You’ll be part of an empowered cross functional go to market team that leverages best practice and seeks continual improvement. You’ll be given the freedom to manage your own time with support and guidance from senior sales leadership. You’ll be expected to build, maintain and report on a clear 12–18 month runway of pipeline with dedicated time set aside each week for strategic focus and execution on new business development.


What you'll need for the role

Smartnumbers values diversity of experience. Candidates should have a strong combination of several of the following skills, competencies and experience: 
 

  • Numbers Obsessed – You live and breathe your pipeline and progress and take pride in its resilience and accuracy.
  • Curious - You want to understand the problems our customers face and how we might solve them. You’re always looking for new opportunities to learn about our customers, the market, competitors, technology, etc.
  • Customer Focused - You start with the customer and work back whilst understanding that solutions have to work for our business
  • Outcome focused - You can define what success looks like and measure progress towards it
  • A clear communicator - You’re capable of explaining things regardless of whether it’s to a software engineer, salesperson, customer support agent or CEO


What we can offer you

As well as a competitive salary of circa £100,000 per annum, we offer a comprehensive benefits package, covering a variety of areas, both professional and personal. These benefits include:  

  • Hybrid working style, with the expectation of two days in the office (with a great City of London office base!)
  • Family friendly benefits including paid parental leave policies
  • An extensive health insurance policy for you, with an option to add your family members 
  • A workplace pension with Hargreaves Lansdown 
  • Life insurance of 4 x your salary 
  • Weekly self-development time to spend exploring your professional development interests
  • 25 days of annual leave (plus bank holidays), your birthday off, and an opportunity to buy up to 5 days annual leave per year
  • A holistic wellbeing support plan encompassing a variety of offerings to assist you. We provide you with a monthly £50 allowance to fund activities to best support your wellbeing as well as workshops and training to provide tools and guidance. Additionally, there is a wide-ranging employee assistance programme available to advise on personal, family or financial matters, and fun social events during the year.


The application process

We have a simple 3 stage application process: 

  1. 30-minute phone call with the hiring manager
  2. 1 hour interview and presentation
  3. HR and Bar Raiser Interview

We welcome all applications for this role.

Company Description

We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.


We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

As an Analytics Manager for Financial Experiences, you will lead analytics for one of Checkout.com’s strategically important product areas. Financial Experiences (FeX) exists to give customers modern solutions to control and manage their money. The product pillar spans products and capabilities across Checkout Business Account and balances, acceleration, FX, financial reporting and invoicing, pricing and billing, bank payouts, and client settlements.

You will be a co-owner of product success in the pillar: shaping how we measure performance, building the data foundations and self-serve products required to support decision-making, and generating insights that influence roadmap priorities and product outcomes.

What you will do

  • You will manage & lead a small team of analytics engineers and product analysts

  • Own the analytics roadmap for FeX, ensuring we are focused on the highest-value opportunities across product measurement, merchant insight, pricing, billing and funds management

  • Define the measurement frameworks, north-star metrics, supporting KPIs, and decision mechanisms that help FeX teams understand whether products are creating value for merchants and for Checkout.com.

  • Partner with Product and Engineering leaders to ensure products are correctly instrumented, the right data is captured, and analytics output is trustworthy, scalable, and actionable.

  • Deliver self-serve data products, dashboards, and analyses that help teams monitor performance, identify product improvement opportunities, and make better trade-offs faster.

  • Increase the data maturity of the pillar by embedding rigorous, data-driven decision-making into discovery, prioritisation, launch measurement, and ongoing product development.

What we’re looking for

  • Experience leading analytics, product analytics, and/or analytics engineering in a product-led environment.

  • Demonstrable experience in building descriptive measurement and delivering insights to evaluate product performance and validate impact.

  • Experience delivering data products, self-serve analytics, and data models that support decision-making at scale.

  • Strong analytical problem-solving skills, with the ability to turn ambiguous business and product questions into clear, structured, data-informed recommendations.

  • Proven ability to work cross-functionally with senior stakeholders, align priorities, and scope analytical delivery in complex environments.

  • Technical foundation in analytics engineering, ideally building data pipelines with DBT, working with cloud data warehouses, scheduling/orchestration of data pipelines

  • Ideally, experience in payments, fintech, financial products, pricing, billing, treasury, or adjacent financial domains.

Additional Information

Bring all of you to work

We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one.

Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands.

We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here.

It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable.

Life at Checkout.com

We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection.

Curious about what it’s like to be part of our team? Visit our Careers Page to learn more about our culture, open roles, and what drives us.

For a closer look at daily life at Checkout.com, follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram

Build AI workflows that Commercial teams actually use and prove the impact. We are looking for a Commercial AI Solutions Specialist to turn high-value Commercial problems into practical, adopted AI workflows.

You will own use cases end to end: discovering problems, assessing and prioritising opportunities, rapidly prototyping solutions, supporting deployment, driving adoption, and measuring business impact. This is a hands-on role for someone who combines curiosity, structured problem-solving, and strong delivery ownership.

You do not need deep expertise in every AI tool or in payments. We do expect evidence that you have learned a new domain quickly, independently built and shipped at least one useful workflow, and translated an ambiguous business problem into a measurable outcome.


What early success looks like

During the first 90 days, you will build a strong understanding of Commercial priorities and workflows, develop a credible pipeline of use cases, and deliver practical quick wins. You will also establish the foundations for measuring adoption, productivity, and commercial impact as the portfolio develops.

By day 90: two workflows live with real Commercial users, each with a named business owner, a measured before/after delta against a pre-build baseline, and sustained weekly active use.

  • Partner with Commercial teams and Revenue Operations to identify workflow pain points and high-value automation and AI augmentation opportunities.

  • Investigate problems, map current processes, establish an evidence-based baseline, and define clear use-case outcomes.

  • Build, test, and rapidly iterate on prototypes using AI-assisted coding tools, automation, and low-code or no-code platforms.

  • Take approved use cases from discovery through deployment, adoption, and impact measurement.

  • Design pragmatic human-in-the-loop workflows, controls, and feedback mechanisms.

  • Coordinate with relevant technical, data, security, and risk partners when a solution requires platform support or formal approval.

  • Support the enablement of end users through clear documentation, demonstrations, training, and ongoing iteration.

  • Maintain visibility of progress, dependencies, risks, adoption, and realised impact.


What we are looking for

  • Evidence of having built and shipped at least one useful workflow, automation, AI-powered tool, or prototype that real users used in practice.

  • Evidence of rapidly learning a new domain or capability and independently delivering a measurable business outcome.

  • Experience owning work from an ambiguous problem through to an implemented solution.

  • Strong analytical and data literacy, including the ability to interpret data, establish baselines, and evaluate outcomes.

  • Hands-on experience building useful workflows, automations, or prototypes using low-code or no-code platforms, automation tools, or AI-assisted coding tools.

  • Structured problem-solving skills and the judgement to distinguish valuable use cases from attractive distractions.

  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence without formal authority.

  • A bias toward action, experimentation, and iteration, balanced with appropriate attention to risk and governance.

  • The ability to work independently while escalating material decisions and dependencies appropriately.

  • Experience in a Commercial, go-to-market, Revenue Operations, payments, fintech, or other regulated-industry environment.

About the role

As an Engineer I, you will support the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of Workday Financials, with a focus on Record to Report (R2R). As Checkout has a complex finance architecture, you will be expected to also develop in learning our P2P system ZIP and Expenses system Emburse.

You will work with Finance and Technology stakeholders to understand requirements, configure and test solutions, investigate issues, and help maintain reliable financial processes and integrations. This is an early-career role for someone with 1–2 years of hands-on Workday Financials experience who is building technical and functional expertise.

What you will be doing

  • Support Workday Financials, ZIP and Emburse development, configuration, maintenance, and optimisation activities.

  • Contribute to Workday R2R processes, including core General Ledger, Financial Accounting, Close and Consolidation, Allocations, Intercompany, Fixed Assets, Taxes, and Financial Reporting.

  • Help gather and clarify business requirements and translate them into practical Workday solutions.

  • Support configuration changes in Workday, following documented design, testing, and change-control practices.

  • Assist with triage and investigation of Workday integration failures, data discrepancies, and process issues.

  • Support financial data flows involving payroll, vendor master data, Accounts Payable in ZIP, and General Ledger postings.

  • Work with Finance stakeholders and technical teams to help deliver reliable, well-documented integrations.

  • Support Workday and ERP release cycles through impact analysis, regression testing, user acceptance testing, and change management.

  • Create and maintain technical documentation, integration runbooks, configuration notes, and knowledge-base content.

  • Monitor recurring issues and contribute to root-cause analysis and continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Research issues independently, document findings, and escalate problems when they exceed defined complexity or access boundaries.

  • Communicate progress, risks, issues, and proposed solutions clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

What you will bring

  • 1–2 years of hands-on experience supporting or delivering Workday Financials.

  • Understanding of core financial processes such as General Ledger, Accounts Payable, period close, allocations, intercompany, or financial reporting.

  • Experience supporting Workday configuration, testing, incident resolution, or release activities.

  • A basic understanding of integrations, data flows, and data quality within enterprise applications.

  • Strong problem-solving skills, including the ability to investigate issues, identify likely root causes, and recommend next steps.

  • A structured and careful approach to configuration, testing, documentation, and change delivery.

  • The ability to understand stakeholder requirements and translate them into clear technical or functional actions.

  • Good written and verbal communication skills, with a customer-focused and collaborative approach.

  • A willingness to learn, develop Workday expertise, and research solutions independently.

Desirable experience

  • Experience with Workday Financials areas such as Financial Accounting, Close and Consolidation, Allocations, Intercompany, Fixed Assets, Taxes, or Financial Reporting.

  • Accounting qualification and experience is desirable

  • Experience supporting payroll, vendor master, Accounts Payable, or General Ledger data flows.

  • Awareness of SOX, audit, data privacy, and control considerations in financial applications.

  • Experience working with Finance users, Technology teams, or implementation partners.

What success looks like

  • Workday Financials issues are investigated thoroughly and progressed with clear evidence.

  • Configuration and integration changes are tested, documented, and delivered in a controlled way.

  • Workday and finance tech processes and related data flows are supported reliably.

  • Requirements, decisions, and known issues are documented clearly.

  • Recurring problems are identified and converted into practical improvement opportunities.

You'll join the Issuing Operations team in London and own the technical side of card issuing deals from first conversation to go-live. Pre-sale, you're front and centre: positioning our issuing platform, building custom card program flows, live demos, and POCs, and winning over the prospect's engineers, product leads, and payments architects while your Account Executive drives the commercial thread. Once the deal is ready, the weight shifts: our Implementation Engineers lead the build and you stay close, ensuring your issuing card program survives contact with reality.

You'll work on a modern, fast-moving platform alongside passionate payments experts across commercial and operations teams.

People who do well here are curious by default: they pull threads, teach themselves what the job needs next, and thrive in fast-paced commercial environments where they act before anyone asks. If that's how you work, you'll like it here.

  • Build & Demonstrate: Run live technical demos, create POCs, and customise technical presentations for developer, operational, and executive audiences alike.

  • Provide Issuing Domain Leadership: Act as an expert on Card Issuing, Program Management, Authorisation & Settlement streams, Network Tokenisation, 3DS, Fraud/Risk Controls, and card program operations.

  • Lead Client Technical Interactions: Lead all technical discussions, from discovery calls and architecture workshops to operational readiness sessions, from first contact through go-live, collaborating closely with Implementation Engineers.

  • Support Complex Procurement (RFPs/RFIs): Support the BID management team on technical, operational, security, and card program design queries in RFP and RFI responses.

  • Voice of the Customer & Operational Feedback: Feed real-world program manager and developer feedback back to Product, Engineering, and Issuing Operations to champion card issuing feature enhancements and process improvements.

  • Industry & Technical Mastery: Maintain deep expertise on Checkout.com’s issuing platform and stay ahead of evolving card scheme rules, issuing infrastructure, and European payment regulations.

  • Full Lifecycle Technical Ownership: Equally comfortable wearing the hat of a pre-sales Solutions Engineer to win complex deals, and driving post-launch technical support, operational health, and incident resolution in production environments, fully owning the 360-degree client relationship from initial discovery through long-term delivery.

About You

Experience

  • 5+ years in a high-velocity, client-facing technical role (Sales Engineer, Solutions Architect, Pre-Sales Consultant, Implementation Engineer, or Technical Account Manager) at a PSP, Card Issuer / Issuer, Processor, Fintech, or Payments company.

  • Proven track record operating directly in fast-paced commercial environments, managing competing deal priorities, and driving commercial momentum alongside sales and operations teams.

  • Mandatory UK & EEA Issuing Experience: Hands-on experience designing, launching, or supporting virtual and physical card programs within the UK and EEA regulatory and scheme landscapes.

  • Issuing Domain Knowledge: Expert understanding of card program mechanics, BIN ranges, issuer processing, and scheme compliance (Visa/Mastercard).

  • Payment Foundations: Strong grasp of end-to-end payment flows, 3DS, Network Tokenisation, Apple/Google Pay, Strong Customer Authentication (SCA), and fraud engine mechanics.

Technical Skills

  • Coding Ability: You can code and are comfortable with web technologies. Proficiency in at least one front-end (JavaScript, React) or back-end language (Node.js, Python, Java, .NET, Go).

  • API & Debugging Mastery: Expert in API-based integrations (REST/JSON, Postman, Webhooks); able to build, reproduce, isolate, and explain technical issues using logs, API responses, and test environments.

How You Work

  • Exceptional Communicator: Clear written and verbal English; equally at home pitching to CTOs and lead architects as you are detailing unit economics and operational flows to CFOs, Operations leads, and C-level stakeholders.

  • Commercially Minded: You talk interchange, authorization rates, card program economics, and revenue impact, not just API endpoints, and proactively push opportunities through the sales funnel.

  • Highly Organised: Thrives under pressure with the ability to prioritise shifting workloads in a fast-moving, deal-driven environment.

Nice to Have

  • Global Issuing Experience: Exposure to launching card programs in global jurisdictions outside the UK/EEA (e.g., US, APAC, LATAM, MENA).

  • Languages: Business fluency in an additional European language.

Pre-sale, you're front and centre: positioning our issuing platform, building custom card program flows, live demos, and POCs, and winning over the prospect's engineers, product leads, and payments architects while your Account Executive drives the commercial thread. Once the deal is ready, the weight shifts: our Implementation Engineers lead the build and you stay close, ensuring your issuing card program survives contact with reality.

You'll work on a modern, fast-moving platform alongside passionate payments experts across commercial and operations teams.

People who do well here are curious by default: they pull threads, teach themselves what the job needs next, and thrive in fast-paced commercial environments where they act before anyone asks. If that's how you work, you'll like it here.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Drive Technical Deal Execution: Partner closely with Sales and Account Managers and the broader Issuing Operations team in high-velocity, high-stakes commercial environments to position Checkout.com’s card issuing platform, winning complex, multi-product deals.

  • Architect Card Issuing Solutions: Understand client requirements across card issuing (virtual and physical cards, funding approaches, balance management, interchange economics as examples) and map them to our APIs and operational workflows to create robust solution designs.

  • Build & Demonstrate: Run live technical demos, create POCs, and customise technical presentations for developer, operational, and executive audiences alike.

  • Provide Issuing Domain Leadership: Act as an expert on Card Issuing, Program Management, Authorisation & Settlement streams, Network Tokenisation, 3DS, Fraud/Risk Controls, and card program operations.

  • Lead Client Technical Interactions: Lead all technical discussions, from discovery calls and architecture workshops to operational readiness sessions, from first contact through go-live, collaborating closely with Implementation Engineers.

  • Support Complex Procurement (RFPs/RFIs): Support the BID management team on technical, operational, security, and card program design queries in RFP and RFI responses.

  • Voice of the Customer & Operational Feedback: Feed real-world program manager and developer feedback back to Product, Engineering, and Issuing Operations to champion card issuing feature enhancements and process improvements.

  • Industry & Technical Mastery: Maintain deep expertise on Checkout.com’s issuing platform and stay ahead of evolving card scheme rules, issuing infrastructure, and European payment regulations.

  • Full Lifecycle Technical Ownership: Equally comfortable wearing the hat of a pre-sales Solutions Engineer to win complex deals, and driving post-launch technical support, operational health, and incident resolution in production environments, fully owning the 360-degree client relationship from initial discovery through long-term delivery.

About You

Experience

  • 5+ years in a high-velocity, client-facing technical role (Sales Engineer, Solutions Architect, Pre-Sales Consultant, Implementation Engineer, or Technical Account Manager) at a PSP, Card Issuer / Issuer, Processor, Fintech, or Payments company.

  • Proven track record operating directly in fast-paced commercial environments, managing competing deal priorities, and driving commercial momentum alongside sales and operations teams.

  • Mandatory UK & EEA Issuing Experience: Hands-on experience designing, launching, or supporting virtual and physical card programs within the UK and EEA regulatory and scheme landscapes.

  • Issuing Domain Knowledge: Expert understanding of card program mechanics, BIN ranges, issuer processing, and scheme compliance (Visa/Mastercard).

  • Payment Foundations: Strong grasp of end-to-end payment flows, 3DS, Network Tokenisation, Apple/Google Pay, Strong Customer Authentication (SCA), and fraud engine mechanics.

  • Coding Ability: You can code and are comfortable with web technologies. Proficiency in at least one front-end (JavaScript, React) or back-end language (Node.js, Python, Java, .NET, Go).

  • API & Debugging Mastery: Expert in API-based integrations (REST/JSON, Postman, Webhooks); able to build, reproduce, isolate, and explain technical issues using logs, API responses, and test environments.

  • Exceptional Communicator: Clear written and verbal English; equally at home pitching to CTOs and lead architects as you are detailing unit economics and operational flows to CFOs, Operations leads, and C-level stakeholders.

We're looking for a Senior Manager, Head of Transaction Monitoring for Checkout.com, based in London.

You will join a growing international Compliance team, reporting into the Head of Financial Crime Controls. This role will lead the global Transaction Monitoring (TM) function, ensuring its effectiveness and scalability while aligning with Checkout.com’s AML policies and regulatory requirements. The role has dual oversight across both first-line (alert investigations) and second-line (FIU and complex investigations) functions, ensuring effective coordination between detection capabilities and investigative processes.

Key responsibilities include leading the TM strategy, building and maintaining the TM framework, coordinating cross-functionally to optimize and enhance detection models, overseeing control effectiveness, and managing both first-line TM operations and second-line financial crime investigations.

The role may also support broader financial crime controls, contributing to the enhancement of other key compliance functions as needed.

  • Lead the global Transaction Monitoring team, providing strategic oversight and technical expertise on AML risk detection and mitigation.

  • Oversee both 1LOD (alert investigations) and 2LOD (FIU and complex investigations), ensuring an effective end-to-end transaction monitoring process with seamless escalation and resolution of financial crime risks.

  • Design, maintain, and continuously improve the TM framework, ensuring a risk-based and scalable approach to transaction monitoring.

  • Work closely with Product and Engineering teams to develop, refine, and optimize transaction monitoring rules and scenarios, ensuring they are effective, calibrated, scalable, and aligned with emerging risks and business growth.

  • Implement quality assurance measures to monitor and enhance the effectiveness of both 1LOD investigations and 2LOD FIU case management.

  • Leverage data analytics and emerging technologies, including AI and machine learning, to enhance detection capabilities and improve efficiency.

  • Ensure compliance with global AML regulations by aligning transaction monitoring policies and processes with industry best practices.

  • Provide subject matter expertise on AML risks to internal stakeholders, supporting risk assessments, audits, and regulatory engagements.

  • Monitor regulatory developments and industry trends to ensure proactive compliance with evolving AML expectations.

  • Lead and develop a high-performing team, fostering a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and innovation.

  • Oversee MI reporting and key performance metrics, ensuring senior leadership has visibility into TM effectiveness, operational efficiency, and escalation trends.

 

What we’re looking for:

  • Minimum 10 years of experience in a senior financial crime/AML role within a regulated financial institution, FinTech, or payments company.

  • Deep understanding of AML transaction monitoring frameworks, financial crime typologies, and regulatory expectations across multiple jurisdictions.

  • Experience overseeing both first-line (alert investigations) and second-line (FIU, complex case investigations) functions.

  • Strong knowledge of payment flows, money laundering risks, in the FinTech/payments sector.

  • Experience working with technology teams to drive improvements in transaction monitoring infrastructure and capabilities.

  • Strong analytical skills and a data-driven mindset, with experience leveraging data to improve monitoring effectiveness.

  • Experience utilizing data analytics, AI, and machine learning to enhance transaction monitoring capabilities.

  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence senior leadership and external regulators.

  • Proactive, strategic thinker with a strong sense of accountability and a solutions-focused approach.

  • Experience leading teams and driving operational excellence within a compliance function.

  • Proficiency in transaction monitoring systems and tools (e.g., Actimize, Mantas, FICO, or equivalent) as well as Microsoft Excel and data visualization platforms.

raw.description:
Company Description

We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.


We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

The Role


This is a newly created role sitting at the centre of some of Checkout.com's most sensitive and consequential regulatory moments. Reporting to the Director of External Affairs, the Senior Manager, Regulatory Inspections and Strategic Response will manage Checkout's most important regulatory situations end-to-end, whether planned or unplanned.

In practice, that means two connected mandates. The first is the planned, cyclical work of running Checkout's regulatory inspections and examinations — a methodical, deadline-driven discipline that forms the steady-state core of the role. The second is the unplanned work: leading the response to the exceptional, time-critical and commercially sensitive situations that require a calm cross-functional leader to bring them to a resolution.

You will be the person the business turns to when a regulator opens an inspection, and when a sensitive cross-functional situation needs to be stabilised quickly and handled with judgement. You will bring order and momentum to ambiguous, high-stakes matters, coordinating across Legal, Compliance, Risk, Commercial, Product, Tech and Communications, and you will own the strategy and the outcome.

This is a role with a clear mandate to build. You will establish the function, set the operating model, and over the course of 2027 hire and develop a small team of specialists to scale it.

What you'll do

Own regulatory inspections end-to-end

  • Act as the single accountable owner for Checkout's regulatory inspections, examinations and skilled-person reviews across the group's regulated entities.

  • Run each inspection as a programme: set the strategy and narrative, build and manage the timeline, coordinate evidence gathering, quality-assure submissions, and prepare and rehearse subject-matter experts and senior stakeholders for regulator engagement.

  • Serve as the primary point of coordination between the business and the regulator.

  • Protect the company's position throughout — controlling disclosures to what is necessary and appropriate, safeguarding confidential supervisory information, and ensuring the executive team and boards are informed at the right moments.

  • Drive continuous improvement by running post-mortems after each engagement and acting on any findings.

Lead the response to sensitive, escalated situations

  • Lead the response to the exceptional, time-critical situations that carry material regulatory, financial or reputation risk and need to be handled at pace.

  • Bring structure to ambiguity: establish the facts, set out the risk and the options for senior decision-makers, secure decisions, assign actions, and maintain momentum until matters are resolved.

  • Work in close partnership with the Director of External Affairs on the most sensitive matters, acting as a trusted extension of the role.

Build the function

  • Establish the operating model and playbooks for a new function within Checkout.com

  • Hire, develop and lead a small team

What we are looking for

  • Significant experience in managing regulatory inspections and engagement - ideally within payments or fintech

  • A methodical, meticulous approach to project management

  • A track record of keeping calm under pressure

  • Highly responsive, solutions-oriented and comfortable operating with ambiguity

  • Commercially pragmatic, with the ability to weigh regulatory and reputational risk against business objectives and to take considered, well-reasoned decisions

  • Excellent stakeholder management: credible with regulators and auditors, trusted by executives, and effective at mobilising colleagues across functions and geographies.

  • People management experience, or clear readiness to build and lead a team

  • Impeccable written communication

Company Description

We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.


We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

The Role


This is a newly created role sitting at the centre of some of Checkout.com's most sensitive and consequential regulatory moments. Reporting to the Director of External Affairs, the Senior Manager, Regulatory Inspections and Strategic Response will manage Checkout's most important regulatory situations end-to-end, whether planned or unplanned.

In practice, that means two connected mandates. The first is the planned, cyclical work of running Checkout's regulatory inspections and examinations — a methodical, deadline-driven discipline that forms the steady-state core of the role. The second is the unplanned work: leading the response to the exceptional, time-critical and commercially sensitive situations that require a calm cross-functional leader to bring them to a resolution.

You will be the person the business turns to when a regulator opens an inspection, and when a sensitive cross-functional situation needs to be stabilised quickly and handled with judgement. You will bring order and momentum to ambiguous, high-stakes matters, coordinating across Legal, Compliance, Risk, Commercial, Product, Tech and Communications, and you will own the strategy and the outcome.

This is a role with a clear mandate to build. You will establish the function, set the operating model, and over the course of 2027 hire and develop a small team of specialists to scale it.

What you'll do

Own regulatory inspections end-to-end

  • Act as the single accountable owner for Checkout's regulatory inspections, examinations and skilled-person reviews across the group's regulated entities.

  • Run each inspection as a programme: set the strategy and narrative, build and manage the timeline, coordinate evidence gathering, quality-assure submissions, and prepare and rehearse subject-matter experts and senior stakeholders for regulator engagement.

  • Serve as the primary point of coordination between the business and the regulator.

  • Protect the company's position throughout — controlling disclosures to what is necessary and appropriate, safeguarding confidential supervisory information, and ensuring the executive team and boards are informed at the right moments.

  • Drive continuous improvement by running post-mortems after each engagement and acting on any findings.

Lead the response to sensitive, escalated situations

  • Lead the response to the exceptional, time-critical situations that carry material regulatory, financial or reputation risk and need to be handled at pace.

  • Bring structure to ambiguity: establish the facts, set out the risk and the options for senior decision-makers, secure decisions, assign actions, and maintain momentum until matters are resolved.

  • Work in close partnership with the Director of External Affairs on the most sensitive matters, acting as a trusted extension of the role.

Build the function

  • Establish the operating model and playbooks for a new function within Checkout.com

  • Hire, develop and lead a small team

  • Significant experience in managing regulatory inspections and engagement - ideally within payments or fintech

  • A methodical, meticulous approach to project management

  • A track record of keeping calm under pressure

  • Highly responsive, solutions-oriented and comfortable operating with ambiguity

  • Commercially pragmatic, with the ability to weigh regulatory and reputational risk against business objectives and to take considered, well-reasoned decisions

  • Excellent stakeholder management: credible with regulators and auditors, trusted by executives, and effective at mobilising colleagues across functions and geographies.

  • People management experience, or clear readiness to build and lead a team

  • Impeccable written communication
